messages.subject: dominant markers and backcross design
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl and All
I have question on how to correctly code the genfile for R/qtl when
dominant markers are used in backcross design. In R/qtl,  it uses AA=1
and AB=2 to code the genotypes in backcross experiment however AA and
AB genotype are indistinguishable when dominant markers like AFLP are
used in genotyping. Also, there is possibility to cross heterozygous F1
back to recessive parent so the progeny will only contain AB (present)
and double recessive BB (absent). We have several backcrosses, they are
all genotyped in dominant DNA markers and some cross are half-sibs
since they share one parent. I have problem to call the genfile
correctly and also let the R/qtl recognize the cross type is backcross.

Thank you so much for your help,

Charles

messages.subject: Re: dominant markers and backcross design
messages.body_plain:
I assume that all backcross progeny were to the A strain, and so all
individuals have genotypes AA or AB.  A marker for which A is
dominant would not be informative and so could be ignored.

karl

messages.subject: Re: trouble with new X chr permutation
messages.subject_clean: trouble with new X chr permutation
messages.body_plain:
The code used to determine the number of permutations for the X
chromosome is the following:

     # X chr versus autosomes
     xchr <- chr.type=="X"
     names(xchr) <- names(cross$geno)

     # chromosome lengths
     L <- summary(pull.map(cross))[,2]
     L <- L[-length(L)]
     La <- sum(L[!xchr])
     Lx <- sum(L[xchr])

     n.perm.X <- ceiling(La/Lx*n.perm)

And so, if you were doing the permutation test with just chr 19 and
X, and used n.perm=1000,
it should run 1162 permutations on the X.

karl

messages.subject: covariates and RILs
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a dataset where we have genotyped the same set of RILs in 3 different environments.  Part of our interests are in environment by QTL interactions.  Currently I analyze each environment differently.  Would it be valid in Rqtl to analyze them together, using the environment as a covariate?  If I were to do this, should I give the RILs in different environments different names (even though they would be the same genotypes).

Thanks for any advice,

Julin

--
Julin Maloof

Section of Plant Biology

University of California, Davis

1 Shields Ave

Davis, CA, 95616

Fax: 530 752 5410

messages.subject: Re: 1 new message in 1 topic - digest
messages.body_plain:
Dear Julin,

It would be a good idea to combine the three environments together,
and concatenating the three sets would be one way to accomplishing
this.  You can look at QTL main effects as well as the QTL-ebvironment
interactions.

One potential problem with the concatenating approach is an artificial
inflation of sample size.  I wonder what Karl thinks about this, and
if there is a way around this in R/qtl right now.

The "right" way would be to fit a random effects model to incorporate
clutsering within lines.

Regards,
Saunak

messages.subject: Re: covariates and RILs
messages.body_plain:
I don't think it is quite right to do this with environment as a
covariate,
because you'd ignore the matching of genotypes across the multiple
environments.
I think it'd be better to treat these as multiple phenotypes, but R/
qtl doesn't
have facilities for that, and so QTL Cartographer might be your best
bet.

karl
